purpose: Revisit the five CAS archive rows held by the initial 21-name crosswalk using current Catalog of Fishes pages and investigate the author-year conflict for Taenioides caeculus. This is nomenclatural research only.

records.sourceStatus: The nominal name Gobius giuris is cited as valid in Glossogobius giurus in Herre (1940, 1946) and as valid in Glossogobius giuris by later treatments; the catalog current status is Valid as Glossogobius giuris (Hamilton 1822).
records.reason: The direct CAS archive preserves the source-reported spelling Glossogobius giurus. The current Catalog of Fishes page supports the accepted name Glossogobius giuris and documents the giurus treatment as a historical combination. Retain the verbatim spelling and use giuris only as the normalized taxon label; this is not specimen re-identification or current-presence evidence.

The current Catalog of Fishes directly treats the source name Hypseleotris agilis as a synonym of Giuris laglaizei. GBIF’s occurrence row retains Giuris margaritacea, so that accepted-name conflict is explicitly preserved and not treated as a specimen re-identification. The source-name-to-current-catalog mapping supports an internal historical assertion only.

The current Catalog of Fishes directly maps Ophiocara aporos to Giuris margaritaceus. GBIF retains the ending margaritacea; preserve that verbatim crosswalk and normalize the internal accepted-name label to the current Catalog spelling. This supports only the dated source-locality record, not specimen re-identification or a current occurrence claim.

The latest Catalog of Fishes treatment accepts Ophiocara porocephalum. The CAS/GBIF rows preserve Ophiocara porocephala, a differing name treatment; retain the verbatim source and GBIF names while using porocephalum as the current normalized label. This is nomenclatural normalization only, with no specimen re-identification or current-presence inference.

The exact CAS IPT row records the species-rank binomial Taenioides caeculus but has no scientificNameAuthorship or identifiedBy value; the 1837 authorship is assigned in GBIF/older ITIS, not stated in the CAS row. The current Catalog of Fishes query for Taenioides caeculus returns no record, while its current entry for the original Valenciennes combination Amblyopus caeculus maps it as a synonym of Taenioides anguillaris (Linnaeus 1758). WoRMS and FishBase likewise treat the formal Bloch & Schneider 1801 Taenioides caeculus name as T. anguillaris. FishBase/CLOFFA distinguish a separate explicitly non-Schneider misapplication associated with T. cirratus; no source evidence links this CAS item to that misapplication. Use T. anguillaris only as a nomenclatural crosswalk, retain the CAS binomial and GBIF label verbatim, and do not interpret this as specimen re-identification, current presence, or a complete checklist.

decision.interpretation: The current Catalog of Fishes supports the fifth source-name crosswalk through Amblyopus caeculus, while preserving the CAS row’s authorless binomial and the older GBIF/ITIS attribution. All 17 exact CAS collection identities now support historical source-locality assertions in the internal research ledger; this is nomenclatural normalization, not specimen re-identification. One MZUSP source item remains held for rank, locality-interpretation and license conflicts. No public species rows, map points, current-presence claim or complete checklist are added.
